newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban form ruling council.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban form ruling council.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic movement announced on Friday an interim ruling council for the country to replace the collapsed government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani.

A declaration issued by the movement's supreme leader Mullah Mohammad Omar hours after Taleban forces captured the capital Kabul named his deputy, Mullah Mohammad Rabbani, no relation of the president, to head the six-man council. It was released by a Pakistan-based Afghan news service.
Omar's declaration, quoted by the private Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) news service, said Rabbani's government had ended and the new council would administer the country for the present.
Mullah Rabbani, deputy leader of the Taleban, was recently the head of the movement's administration in eastern provinces.
The five other council members are: Mullah Mohammad Hassan, Mullah Abdul Razzaq, Maulvi Shamsuddin, Mullah Mohammad Ghaus and Mullah Mohammad Fazil.
